name: selector-pin-repair
title: Repair stale counted evidence selector pins without discarding proven receipts
description:
A waiver is currently justifying itself by pointing at a follow-up that did not exist. Both B-9ff1 waivers assert the tooling gap 'is filed as its own task'; the test-coverage reviewer searched story_list and bug_list during B-9ff1's closing review and found no such story or bug. This story makes that claim true and fixes the gap it names.

The gap: a pinned (command, selector) evidence pin is immutable by design, which is what makes the receipt trustworthy - a caller cannot retroactively rewrite what was proven. But when the pinned selector literal contains a COUNT ('7 invocations', '25 fixtures') the next fixture addition strands it: the command still passes, the behaviour is still proven, and the only available disposition is a waiver that throws away the coverage claim. Two B-9ff1 intents are in exactly that state, both independently confirmed by re-running the harnesses (7 -> 8 invocations, 25 -> 33 fixtures).

This is deliberately scoped as a real story rather than a chore because any repair path is a hole in the immutability the subsystem depends on, and it must be shown NOT to launder a failing intent into a passing one.
source: B-9ff1 closing review (test-coverage lane, RP-034): both waivers claim a filed follow-up task that did not exist
